domain_symbols.robotics: robot kinematics, dynamics, control, and planning
domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: Denavit-Hartenberg link transform
rules.input_form: DH parameters (a_i, alpha_i, d_i, theta_i) for link i
rules.operation: Build the homogeneous link transform from the four Denavit-Hartenberg parameters.
examples: A 6-DOF arm forward kinematics is product A_1 * A_2 * ... * A_6
counterexamples: Mixing classical and modified DH conventions in one chain
common_errors: Forgetting that theta is the joint variable for revolute joints, d for prismatic

rules.name: Forward kinematics chain product
rules.input_form: joint vector q and link transforms A_i(q)
rules.operation: Compose link transforms in chain order to obtain the end-effector pose.
examples: End-effector position is the upper-right 3x1 block of T_0^n
counterexamples: Reversing chain order gives the inverse pose

rules.name: Geometric Jacobian (linear/angular)
rules.input_form: joint axes z_i and origin positions o_i along chain
rules.output_form: J(q) = [ [z_i x (o_n - o_i)] over [z_i] ] for revolute joints
rules.operation: Assemble the 6xN geometric Jacobian relating joint rates to end-effector twist.
examples: v = J(q) * qdot maps joint velocities to spatial twist
counterexamples: Prismatic columns use [z_i; 0] rather than the revolute form
common_errors: Using analytic Jacobian when geometric is required for force/twist mapping

rules.name: Inverse kinematics singularity test
rules.operation: Detect kinematic singularities via Jacobian rank deficiency.
examples: A 6R arm at full extension loses one twist direction
common_errors: Computing pseudo-inverse without damping near singularities causes joint blow-up

rules.name: Newton-Euler recursive dynamics
rules.input_form: joint state (q, qdot, qddot), inertial parameters
preconditions: Inertia tensors and link masses known
rules.operation: Forward-recurse velocities/accelerations, backward-recurse forces and torques to compute inverse dynamics in O(n).
examples: Used for real-time torque control and gravity compensation
counterexamples: Lagrangian formulation gives same tau but with O(n^4) naive cost
common_errors: Omitting Coriolis terms when qdot is nonzero

rules.name: Manipulator equation of motion
rules.output_form: M(q) qddot + C(q,qdot) qdot + g(q) = tau
preconditions: M positive definite, C consistent with dM/dt = C + C^T
rules.operation: Express robot dynamics in the standard mass-Coriolis-gravity form for control design.
examples: Computed-torque control inverts this equation to linearize
counterexamples: External contact wrench adds J^T F term on the right
common_errors: Choosing C inconsistent with the skew-symmetry property

rules.name: PID control law
rules.output_form: u(t) = Kp e(t) + Ki integral(e) dt + Kd de/dt
rules.operation: Apply proportional-integral-derivative feedback to track a reference signal.
examples: Joint position tracking on a servo motor

rules.name: Linear quadratic regulator
rules.input_form: linear system xdot = A x + B u with cost integral(x^T Q x + u^T R u) dt
rules.output_form: u = -K x where K = R^{-1} B^T P, P solves CARE
rules.operation: Solve the continuous algebraic Riccati equation to obtain the optimal infinite-horizon LQR gain.
counterexamples: Nonlinear systems require iterative LQR or MPC
common_errors: Treating Q as identity by default without weighting physical units

rules.name: Discrete Kalman filter update
rules.input_form: prior (x_k|k-1, P_k|k-1), measurement z_k, model H, R
rules.output_form: K = P H^T (H P H^T + R)^{-1}; x_k|k = x_k|k-1 + K (z - H x_k|k-1); P_k|k = (I - K H) P_k|k-1
rules.operation: Fuse a measurement with a prior estimate to produce the minimum-variance posterior.
examples: Sensor fusion of IMU and GPS
common_errors: Using non-symmetric P due to numerical roundoff

rules.name: RRT path planning probabilistic completeness
rules.output_form: P(success) -> 1 as n -> infinity if solution exists
rules.operation: Use Rapidly-exploring Random Trees to sample-grow a tree biased toward unexplored regions.
counterexamples: RRT is not optimal; use RRT* for asymptotic optimality
common_errors: Sampling near goal too aggressively causes local-minimum bias

rules.name: Trapezoidal velocity trajectory
rules.input_form: displacement L, max velocity vmax, max acceleration amax
rules.output_form: piecewise (accel, cruise, decel) profile with total time T
rules.operation: Generate a time-optimal trapezoidal velocity profile under acceleration and velocity bounds.
examples: Triangular profile if L < vmax^2 / amax
counterexamples: Discontinuous acceleration causes jerk spikes; use S-curve when smoothness matters
common_errors: Ignoring jerk limits in mechanical systems with compliance

rules.name: EKF-SLAM measurement update
rules.input_form: robot pose x_r and landmark positions x_L joint state
rules.operation: Maintain a joint Gaussian over robot pose and landmarks; update with each observation.
counterexamples: EKF-SLAM is inconsistent under wrong data association
common_errors: Quadratic memory growth with landmark count
